Each entry's survey is the output of `node scripts/dossier_corpus.mjs --survey <owner/name> <commit>` on 2026-11-24, which applies the structure record's own rules (packages/polaris-dossier/src/derive.ts, server-entry@1, docs-tree@1, manifest-names@1) to the listing with no secret-path predicate

mechanismVersion.encoding: SHA-256 of the text `polaris-dossier-mechanism/1` and a newline, then one line `<sha256 of the file's bytes>  <path>` per member file, sorted by path (code units), each ending in a newline. A member with `*` names every file in its directory whose name matches, less those ending in an excluded suffix; a member naming no file refuses. Computed by mechanismVersion (packages/polaris-dossier/src/corpus.ts), printed by `node scripts/dossier_corpus.mjs --digest`
mechanismVersion.covers: What an author is told (brief, reader standards, shape packs), may write (draft schema), is checked against (check and the structure rules it derives from), is rendered as (renderer), and what is screened out of reach (screen and the declared-source policies). Not covered, so a change there starts no pass: session prompts and the supervisor (polaris.ts, session-handover.ts), review packets and verdict reading (review*.ts), the inventory, census and every module these import. A cosmetic change to a covered file (a comment) does move the digest

passBudget.passDue: A pass is due when the mechanism version differs from the last pass's. At most one pass starts per ISO week (UTC); a pass runs at the mechanism version of the commit it starts from, and a change during a pass starts no second one
passBudget.rerunWhen: Only a run the runner records as an infrastructure fault (provider outage or refusal, host restart, a runner defect) is run again, once; the failed attempt stays a recorded result. A run that ends for any other reason is the result

perRun.sessions: the four the supervisor starts (author, inventory, fidelity review, design review), no more

plainArm.reach: the whole clone minus detector matches (the owner's 2026-11-21 answer), public entries only

perPass.tokenBudgetBasis: 15,000,000 tokens (half the per-run ceiling) for each of the 28 runs of fourteen entries, plus 5,000,000 for each of the 13 plain-arm sessions: 420,000,000 + 65,000,000

passBudget.whenSpent: When the pass's wall hours or token budget is spent, no further run or session starts; a running one finishes under its own limits. Every entry or arm not reached is recorded Unknown with the reason `pass-budget-spent`, never as a pass or a fail

passRule.verdictRule: A pass's generality verdict is `pass` when every clause below holds for every entry; `fail` when any clause fails for any entry; otherwise `incomplete` (some clause is Unknown and none fails). An Unknown is never a pass (VIS-2)

clauses.statement: Both runs of the entry reach a reviewed close (the run closes with a fidelity verdict and a design verdict recorded) within the per-run limits. One of two closing fails the clause; the result says which

Public entries only. For each of the six question kinds (purpose, structure, mechanism, rationale, change, limits), the dossier's reader share is the mean over its two runs, and it is below the plain arm's when it is lower by more than one required fact of that kind (A-63's per-kind bar, 1/n for a kind with n facts in the entry's key). The clause holds when at most one kind is below. With no key for the entry, or no plain-arm session, the clause is Unknown. The synthetic entry has no plain arm and the clause does not apply to it
Every required view of the figure policy is present or omitted with a stated reason in both runs: zero missing. Unknown until the figure policy's coverage row exists in the scorecard

In both runs every Pole carries at least one cited choice and at least one cited trade-off or limit, the dossier carries at least one worth-knowing mark, and its top-ten coverage is at least 0.7. Unknown until the scorecard's depth rows exist

Each run records which traits matched no shape pack and which units were left derived-only (or that the scale ladder is not built). A run that records neither fails the clause: a thin dossier must be a named gap

calibration.statement: Each pass seeds nine known-false blocks into one copy of one review packet (never a dossier) and records how many the fidelity reviewer flags. Below seven, every readiness verdict of that pass reads `uncalibrated`; the generality verdict is unchanged

baseline.tokensWhy: Unknown: none of the six stored runs recorded usage figures at close (usageFiguresGivenAtClose 0 in each)

costTargets.statement: Wall time: the median of the cost-baseline-anchor entry's runs is at most 0.7 of the baseline median (31.325 minutes); review rounds: its median is at most three. The baseline is one repository, so the like-for-like comparison is that repository; the pass-wide medians are reported beside it against the same figures and decide nothing. Tokens: the baseline is Unknown, so the token target is 0.7 of the first pass's anchor median, fixed in that pass's record before the second pass starts. Cost targets judge from the second pass; the first pass reports them
costTargets.refreshTarget: When R14's refresh exists: a refresh of a dossier whose cited spans changed by under ten percent costs at most a third of a full run's tokens and wall time. Unknown until then

regression.statement: Between two passes, an entry regresses when (a) it met G1 before and fails it now, or (b) its reader share falls in both runs against the previous pass's two-run mean: overall by more than five points, or in one kind by more than one required fact, or by a full fact in each of three or more kinds (A-63). A drop in one run only is reported as noise and is not called a regression; no rise is called a win (A-38 rule 3)

passRule.goalposts: This rule, the entries, the tiers, the mechanism-version definition and the budget are sealed (seal below). A pass record names the corpus version and the seal it ran under, and a pass is judged only by the rule it started under. Changing a sealed member is a new corpus file (dossier-corpus-v2.json) with its own adoption row, applying to passes that start after it lands; this file is never edited in place
